details.label: Summary
details.text: Multiple areas of strong-to-severe thunderstorms capable of damaging winds will continue this evening and into the overnight hours

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Multiple clusters of strong-to-severe thunderstorms are ongoing across portions of the Mid-Atlantic this evening and should continue into the overnight. One such cluster is the remnants of a small bowing segment that moved southeast out of Pennsylvania and is currently approaching Baltimore, MD. Another, larger cluster, is stretched along a line from easter West Virginia, northern Virginia, and parts of Maryland and moving south-southeast. A third area extends northwest to southeast from northern Virginia toward southern Chesapeake Bay area. The environment across the region remains unstable with MUCAPE ranging from 2000-3000 J/kg with deep-layer shear around 35 knots, which will be more than sufficient to sustain thunderstorms into the overnight hours. Additionally, despite low-level lapse rates being weaker than during the afternoon/evening, DCAPE values around 1000-1200 J/kg will be more than sufficient for damaging outflow winds and perhaps a couple damaging downbursts. At present the most likely corridor of damaging wind potential looks to be along and ahead of the linear MCS moving south-southeast across northern Virginia. This region looks to remain west of the developing warm-air advection showers, is largely undisturbed by previous convection, and lies ahead of a sufficiently organized MCS that has a history of producing wind damage. A southwestward extension of Severe Thunderstorm Watch #652 may be necessary
